english: Well, if it ain't me favorite scrag. Come to lick the shite off me boots like a good [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)], have we?
Or mayhap you're one of them as have been chasing ill rumors regarding a certain wild-eyed Hellsguard─the same one they say's been making his bloody mark with the Company of Heroes of late.

Don't tell me you haven't heard of the Company. A hard band of bastards and brigands, they be─of the like this realm ain't never seen. Can't visit an alehouse, souphouse, or whorehouse in this town without having your ears crammed full of fanciful tales 'bout stronghold raidings and primal slayings.

Yet there are those who've walked the Lance into Dravania with naught but a knife in their pocket and come back with the head of a hoary drake─only to be denied admittance to the Company. The fact that this stripling won a seat amongst that lot not five turns of the sun after rapping on their gates...well, that there be the true mystery.
That is, a mystery to them as ain't never heard the legends of the Hellsguard warriors.

Bards still sing of a time when whole cities were leveled by a handful of their kind. Like wild beasts, they were. The sound of their roaring alone would make stout knights soil themselves, and lesser men hide behind their whores.
More's the bloody pity, too. With the Empire breathing down our necks, we could do with knowing exactly how a handful of men could butcher an army or ten.

Speaking of which...mayhap this lad from the Farreach knows something of how they got the job done...and if he does, might be as someone could persuade him into giving the rest of us a few pointers, like.

If he was here, I'd grab the scrag by the scruff of his dirty neck and bleed his secrets out of him, o' course! But lo, I've me duties to think of, and the cap'n would tan me hide and use it to patch his codpiece if he learned I'd left me post. So, I suppose that just leaves you, eh? Swear to me you'll seek the lad out and let us know if he's the genuine article, and I'll tell you where to look for him. Sounds fair, don't it?
Hmph. No hair off my arse.

It's settled then. The man calls himself Curious Gorge, and he's said to have set up camp in a cave to the southeast of Camp Horizon. In western Thanalan, it is. I'd tell you more, but that's as much as any bugger knows. Still, you adventurers ain't exactly short of a bit of resourcefulness, so I'm sure you'll manage.

And now folks won't stop going on about their latest bloody recruit─some flame-skinned Roegadyn come down from the forsaken crags of the Farreach, apparently. Few have actually laid eyes on the man, but them as have reckon his veins must course with the blood of the Fury, for none can stay his axe once he takes the field.
And then, one day, they simply up and vanished from the realm, taking the secrets of their success with them.
Thought I smelled something rank. Another young whelp fresh from [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] mammy's pap come looking to play pirates, eh?

I ain't never been to Thanalan meself, but I hear it's hotter than a forge, and dryer than a crone's...well, you get the idea[@IF($E9(4), missy,)]. If it be solitude the lad wants, he sure as hells chose the right bloody place.
What? I ain't got words to mince with whelps...unless that is, you're here to become a wolf.
If that's the case, then I'm Curious Gorge─but one remark about the name and I'll rip that [@IF($E9(4),pretty,ugly)] head from your shoulders and suck the marrow out of your twitching spine.

Ahem. Now, I suppose you've heard the rumors about a bloodthirsty madman who, using lost battle techniques, has left a gruesome trail of carnage from Ablathia's Spine to the Sagolii Desert? Aye, well, they're all true─except for the parts about the carnage. Those have been greatly understated.
That the techniques are “lost” is also untrue, for my tribe has been handing them down for thousands of years.

Yet though our numbers dwindle with every new summer, the elders refuse to accept new acolytes from outside the village, apparently content to let the art die with us. This is why I left the mountain in which I was raised and came here─to spread the teachings of the warrior in hopes that the techniques will be passed on to future generations.

If you wish, I can teach those techniques to you, but first I must measure whether your body and spirit have the capacity to bear such a burden. To walk the path of the warrior, one must call upon the primal instincts that slumber within the soul.
To the north of this cave you will find an antling nest. Prove to me that you fear not the cries of battle, nor shun the call of death. Do this, and my knowledge is yours.
The inner beast awaits. Wake [@IF($E9(4),her,him)] from [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] slumber and embrace [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] power.
However, without a tempered mind and steely resolve, those instincts would engender such rage as could drive a man to madness.

Any [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] can take up an axe and call [@IF($E9(4),herself,himself)] a marauder, but to become a true warrior, [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] must prove [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] can tame the inner beast that guides the blade. Slay the foul antlings who make their nest to the north of this cave and prove that your will is stone. Do this, and my knowledge is yours.
I witnessed your battle with the antlings, and must say that I was surprised. You have proven yourself far more worthy of this than I could have imagined.

In your hands lies the Soul of the Warrior─a crystal within which the deeds of a thousand thousand warriors from history are recorded. For countless generations, the Soul has been passed on to those in my tribe who choose the path of the warrior, to guide them and aid them on their journey.
When your inner beast awakens, the runes will resonate, further empowering your will, and granting you such strength as you never thought possible.

Today, there is cause for celebration, my friend, for through you, I have ensured that my tribe's legacy will endure. This is why I left my home. This is why I joined the Company of Heroes. This is why I am here today.
Yet however hard I try, and however earnestly I pursue my goal, I cannot deny that I believe that my mission will ultimately end in failure.
While I style myself a warrior, the truth is that I left the mountains long before my training was complete.
And while I carry with me the chronicles of my ancestors, detailing the ancient arts of war, I lack the ability to decipher the texts.
Yet, there may still be hope, for there is another who fled my village─one who shared my dream of passing on the teachings of the tribe, and [@1A(1)]can[@1A(0)] read the tome... My brother.
Without him, I fear there is little more I can teach you at this time.
But that will not discourage me from continuing my studies of the chronicles, nor shake my belief that further secrets will soon reveal themselves to me.
The next warrior quest will be available from Curious Gorge upon reaching level 35.

Until then, I ask that you use the knowledge I've passed on to you, and continue your training. You must strive to harden your will so that it may endure the strain of future burdens. Good luck, my friend.

Well, throw me in the fire and call me Rosy! You're back! What with you taking so long, I naturally made you for an oath-breaking cur, and was planning on sending the lads 'round to gut you! 'Tis lucky there were a few names higher up on me list, eh!? Heh heh!

Hmm... This warrior lad sounds interesting...which means the cap'n will definitely want to hear about him...which means someone'll be getting extra rum rations tonight! Heh heh heh! Much obliged, scrag! Now bugger off!

Welcome back, my friend. Much has happened in the short span since last we spoke.

These past several turns of the sun, my duties with the Company of Heroes have taken me back and forth across the realm in search of a mysterious feral beast that's been terrorizing the smallfolk. People know not whence this monstrosity came, but witnesses say its thirst for blood is unlike anything they've ever seen.
Unfortunately, the time I have spent in pursuit of the beast is time I have not spent studying the chronicles, and I am sorry to say I have made little progress.

However, while on the road, I was able to decipher one passage that may be of interest to us both. From what I can gather, the chronicles tell of an ancient set of armor forged by my ancestors in the flames of the seven hells, and inscribed with the same arcane incantations that adorn the Soul of the Warrior.

Apparently, this mighty armor was passed down from hero to apprentice for centuries, until one man, driven by rage and vainglory, cast all five pieces from Ablathia's highest peak. Since that day, the armor has remained lost...and with it, the power that it harbors.

As far as I can make out, the next passage in the chronicles concerns the whereabouts of the missing artifacts...though I have only been able to make sense of the odd word thus far. Still, I must confess to some excitement. It may well be that the pieces cannot be found, of course, but if they [@1A(1)]could[@1A(0)]...imagine what a warrior thus clad could achieve!
Ah, if only my brother were here... We could decipher the text together and spread the teachings of our people to the entire realm!
Alas, he is not. His whereabouts are as hidden to me as those of the ancient armor. I would have liked you to meet him...if only so that you could have looked upon a true warrior.

Well, perhaps you still shall. Eorzea is not as large as most people perceive. Paths cross, fates intertwine. Such is the will of the Spinner. It may be that my brother has chosen a similar path to mine. It may be that─
Ah, but enough of my rambling. I shall not tire you with my words any longer. You are here to take the next step in your training, and so I shall oblige.

Far to the north, beyond the boundaries of this forsaken desert, lies the Black Shroud. In a corner of this primeval wood can be found an area which the locals have dubbed “Humblehearth,” and it is here that a deadly hunter lurks─Sirocco.

When facing this cold-blooded creature, you will soon realize that the labored swings of your axe are ill-suited to the task of felling such a nimble foe─but do not let this dissuade you from your mission. Wake the slumbering beast within and allow it to guide your hand. Learn to anticipate the movements of your mark, and wheresoever it leaps, be there to meet it with your killing edge.
I understand that you may require more time for preparation. Speak with me again when you have steeled your resolve.

Excellent. I sense your will growing stronger with every step you take. Here, accept this linkpearl. It will allow me to contact you when I have finished my next round of deciphering. Better that than have you make the long journey here on the off[@1F]chance that my studies have borne fruit. Good luck, and may the Fury be with you.
Deciphering the chronicles is proving to be a much more demanding task than I had imagined. I shall continue my work, but ask that you be patient.
The next warrior quest will be available from Curious Gorge upon reaching level 35.
Sirocco is said to hunt with its mate─the female acting as a decoy while he circles to subdue his prey from behind.

He is an agile creature who will use his speed to dodge the deliberate blows of your axe. But if you can wake your inner beast, it will help you anticipate your mark's movements, allowing you to situate your blade directly in Sirocco's path the moment he arrives.

Luck was not with us, because the next moment, we found ourselves in the middle of a riot. Drunken hunters were firing arrows into the crowd, and we were caught between them. Rule one: ye gather yerself a party of between [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] and [@IF($E5(8,0),[@IF($E2(8,10),[@SWITCH(8,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(8)])],[@VALUE(8)])]. Ye ain't no use to us dead, and there's strength t' be had in numbers.[@CR]Rule two: anythin' ye find in the Darkhold is property o' the Faces o' Mercy 'til we tells ye otherwise. Anyone caught tryin' t' smuggle stuff out will get taken t' the Sea o' Clouds fer a nice swim.[@CR]Rule three: let us know of anyone in yer party unwise enough t' try a spot o' smugglin', and yer reward fer the mission is doubled.

Take this [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000269,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000269,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] and show it t' the House Dzemael guard posted at the Darkhold's entrance. He's one of us, and will give ye the particulars of what's waitin' fer ye inside.

To enter the Dzemael Darkhold, you must be in a party of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] to [@IF($E5(8,0),[@IF($E2(8,10),[@SWITCH(8,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(8)])],[@VALUE(8)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE($E8(4))] or higher.

And that mission is bringin' back an imperial centurion's [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000270,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000270,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. Don't care how ye come by it, so long as ye do, and it's in workin' order.

I have sworn on the ancient sigil of House Dzemael not to grant any person, be he of common or noble birth, passage into the Darkhold. Begone or I shall deliver you from this place by for─ Here on behalf of the Faces of Mercy? Well, then, it seems I owe you an apology. You must forgive me. My station requires that I follow a certain protocol.

Very well then. You have your orders from your contact. Carry them out as you see fit, but keep in mind the three rules you were told. I suggest that you exercise caution upon entering the Darkhold. Imperial soldiers will not be the only danger you face down there. The shadows hide other...more sinister creatures. Engage only what you must, and avoid what you can, if you wish to come back alive.

The depths of the Darkhold are said to contain a rift through which the creatures of the void gain entrance to this realm. And they are not all that passes through. Foul miasmas seep into the caverns, clogging the lungs and poisoning the minds of any who linger too long.

After completing an expedition in the Dzemael Darkhold, you will not be permitted to return to the area immediately. To confirm how long you must wait before re-entering, view the Timers tab located under Attributes in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)].

To ensure that the noisome mists are not allowed the opportunity to tighten their grip, I shall be casting a spell upon you that will teleport you back here to my side after the passing of several bells.
You can remain in the Dzemael Darkhold for a maximum of [@VALUE($E8(2))] minutes (Earth time) per visit.
In addition to the spell, you may leave the Darkhold at your leisure by returning to the entrance on foot.

Previous expedition parties reported finding what they called a “magitek terminal” deep in farthest reaches of the lower chambers. It is said the device can instantly return a man to this spot, but during my dealings with the Faces of Mercy, I have found it best to take such tales with a grain of salt.

Oh, and should you come to grief down there, former visitors have confirmed that using a Return spell will transport you back to the Darkhold's entrance, so you may continue your mission, if you so wish.
And that is all the information I can give you. If I may offer an opinion, though─this is an evil place, forsaken by the Twelve and embraced by devils. Leave while you still can, and don't look back.
But seeing as you will not, the least I can do is offer you one last opportunity to make your final preparations. Speak to me once more when you are ready.
All items in a player's loot list will automatically be transferred to that player's inventory upon leaving the dungeon. Items unable to be obtained will be lost.
Enter Dzemael Darkhold?
Thought better of it, have we? Then why do I still have the feeling you'll be back?
I see you could not be swayed. Very well.
Still amongst the living, are we? Then you have fared better than most who venture into the Darkhold, and for that, I salute you.
Made it back in one piece, I see. Ye're either strong as an aurochs, or swift as an antelope. Don't matter which, o'course, as long as ye got the job done. So, did ye?

Ah, yes, [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000270,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000270,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. Ye've done well, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]. This here piece of Garlean wizardry'll come in right handy.

Ain't got the first bloody clue how these things work, but we saw the imperials usin' 'em t' find crystals buried in rocks an' crags, an' that got us to thinkin' [@1A(1)]we[@1A(0)] might try usin' 'em t' find crystals buried in rocks an' crags, see? A cunnin' plan an' no mistake! Heh heh heh!

Since the Empire arrived and started gatherin' up all the realm's crystals, crafters've been scramblin' t' buy any they can get their hands on. A sack of fire or wind can fetch a man ten times what it did just a moon ago.
Hm? What do the imperials want with crystals when they got 'emselves ceruleum? Well, ye can't summon a primal with a pot o' blue piss now, can ye?
Aye, ye heard me right. The Garleans are lookin' to rouse 'em a beast god, and from what I can make out, a bloody nasty one, at that. I'll let ye try an' guess what they plan on doin' with it.
Why, considerin' all that, I'd say seein' to the timely disembowelment of a few imperials an' righteously reappropriatin' their tools might very well count as a service t' the realm!
Aye, ye've done well, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)], an' the Faces o' Mercy won't soon forget it.
How'd I know ye was sharin' sheets with the 'Cudas? Simple. That slippery scrag Hasthwab sent ye. Oh, but tell him not t' worry─his secret's safe with me. Heh heh heh!

Ye can keep all that ye found in the Darkhold, less the [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000270,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000270,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], o'course. Now scurry off back t' yer Admiral. Chances are, she's worried sick.
Back so soon? I trust you found a way into the Darkhold? Tell me, what did you discover?
What is this talk of a primal!? Absurd!

Yes, legend says these demigods worshipped by the beast tribes feed on the aetheric energy trapped within crystals, and yes, if the Garleans [@1A(1)]were[@1A(0)] to have discovered a way to summon the creatures, it is only logical to assume that they would require an absurd amount of manifested aether─an amount found only in areas like Mor Dhona, the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak, and the Dzemael Darkhold...
The Garleans' loathing for the beast tribes and their deities is well known. They've repeatedly attempted [@1A(1)]genocide[@1A(0)], for heaven's sake!

Yet even if this proves to be a mere falsehood conceived by the Faces of Mercy, the Admiral and her advisors must be informed. In the meantime, our investigation of the Darkhold must continue. It troubles me that this Quiliane so easily saw through a disguise that has served us for nigh on five summers, but from what I gathered from your story, she needs our help as much as we need hers. For the moment, we shall refrain from severing our ties with her organization, but we must take extra care not to reveal anything that may be used against us.
Congratulations on another assignment completed, recruit. Here are the Storm Seals you were promised.
But even if it were all true, why do it?

Ah, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)], impeccable timing as ever. The Maelstrom has need of a dependable operative for a covert mission, and your name was foremost in my mind.

We've received reports that an individual claiming knowledge of how to defeat primals has appeared in Gridania, a man said to be the leader of a fraternity called the Circle of Knowing. As if to confirm our intelligence, the Gridanians have since extended to us an offer of alliance, proposing that we act in concert to eliminate Ifrit, under the direction of the aforementioned third party.

Hah! Those wooden-headed tree fondlers will have to do better than [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] if they hope to play the thalassocracy! All know it was our own Company of Heroes that slew Leviathan, and it's plain the Gridanians seek to supplement their feeble ranks with allies who might feasibly contend with a primal.
Needless to say, we stand to gain little and less by joining hands with such cravens. Yet it cannot be denied that the secrets held by this man─this Louisoix─may prove useful to us.

Assuming he isn't a Gridanian fabrication, of course─bait to lure our trust and thence our resources. I mean, if this Louisoix truly [@1A(1)]were[@1A(0)] the leader of those who advocated the reformation of the Maelstrom, would he not make Limsa Lominsa his first port of call?

And here, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)], is where your services are required. We need you to verify the identity of Louisoix and ascertain if he does indeed know of a means to defeat Ifrit. Should all appear to be in order, you are to [@1A(1)]invite[@1A(0)] him to Limsa Lominsa.
Louisoix has taken up residence in Gridania, and is said to frequent Apkallus Falls. Take yourself there, and be on the lookout for an elderly Elezen man.

In order to discern whether Louisoix is who he claims to be, you will need to encourage the man to talk. And to encourage him to talk, you must gain his trust. Do whatever is necessary to earn his confidence, even if it means offering to fight Ifrit himself.

Should it come to that, you will want to assemble a party of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] before facing the primal. Battling the Lord of the Inferno with fewer would be tantamount to suicide.

This mission is of the utmost gravity to the Maelstrom, and I'm loath to entrust it to any other. I would ask you to reconsider, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)].

Not even the prospect of facing a primal makes you flinch. I'm glad to count you among our ranks, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)]. Now, without further ado, go forth and make the Maelstrom proud!

Only parties consisting of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE(25)] or above will be permitted to battle the primal Ifrit.

One last thing. The secrecy of this mission is a matter of national security. As such, if you are able to accomplish this task aided only by sworn members of the Maelstrom─and no outsiders─I shall see to it that you are rewarded more generously.

Only parties consisting of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE(25)] or above will be permitted to battle the primal Ifrit.

Ah, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)], you come at a most opportune time. I was just about to send for you, to discuss a mission of considerable gravity.

Mayhap you have heard of the fellowship that was the driving force behind our organization's revival. Well, the leader of this group happens to be sojourning in Gridania at this very moment, a wise man named Louisoix Leveilleur.
He comes to us from a remote island far to the north, where he has devoted himself to the mastery of all knowledge. 'Tis said there is no subject in the world in which he is unversed.
And now he graces us with his presence, traveling long malms and risking countless perils that we might avail ourselves of his knowledge on how to defeat the primals.

Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna has already held audience with Louisoix, following which she declared that Gridania will offer to join with the Ul'dahns in a joint strike against Ifrit, the primal of fire.
In so doing, an alliance might be established with the sultanate─one that will hopefully come to encompass Limsa Lominsa in time. Such is the will of Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna and the Circle of Knowing.

And now we come to your role in this. Your task, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)], will be to assist Louisoix directly. Our guest is an elderly Elezen gentleman. Meet with him at Apkallus Falls, and attend well his every word, that you might arm yourself with the knowledge to overcome Ifrit.

Be warned, however, that primals are not opponents to be taken lightly─one [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] alone cannot hope to defeat the Lord of the Inferno. You must hand-pick your most trusted companions and with them form a party of four for the battle.

Further, barring exceptional circumstances, we ask that you seek the aid of none but those sworn to the Order of the Twin Adder. If the secret to vanquishing primals is known only to our organization, the other nation-states will be all the more likely to enlist our aid, bringing Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna's dream of a three[@1F]nation alliance that much closer to being.
Now, we are not unmindful that such constraints render an already onerous mission that much more difficult. As such, we are prepared to offer you an incentive by way of further rewards.

I understand full well your apprehension. It is no small thing to vie with a god. But our number counts none more suited to the task. For the sake of our forest nation and all who call it home, I beg you reconsider.

Your mission is a crucial first step towards realizing the Elder Seedseer's dream of a three[@1F]nation alliance. My thanks, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)], and may the Twelve speed your way.

Only parties consisting of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE(25)] or above will be permitted to battle the primal Ifrit.

[@IF($E1($E9(54),0),[@IF($E3($E9(54),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(54),14)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)], just the [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] I was looking for. Tell me, do you know of the primal Ifrit?
[@1A(1)]Seen[@1A(0)] him, you say!? I'm impressed. You obviously like to keep yourself occupied while out in the field.
No doubt you already know that Ifrit is the primal worshipped by the Amalj'aa. And you will know too that he bestows his protection upon the lizardmen.
The primals are otherworldly beings said to answer the call of those who are strong of will. Before such stalwart souls do they appear to bestow their protection.

The Amalj'aa worship a primal named Ifrit, known also as the Lord of the Inferno. Rumor holds that mortals who feel the touch of his fiery breath are rendered his thralls unto death. A dreadful fate, I'm sure you'll agree.
Now, according to the thaumaturges, Ifrit has been gaining strength of late. They've theorized that the changes occurring to Dalamud in recent moons are symptoms of the primal's burgeoning might.

The other city[@1F]states are conducting investigations as we speak in an attempt to discover the explanation for this phenomenon. Unsurprisingly, they've made next to no progress─it has yet to occur to the simple minds of those boorish pirates and tree-worshippers that the answer may be somewhat closer to home.
Do you see where this is going?[@CR]...No? Then allow me to expound.
By proving the connection between Ifrit and Dalamud, Ul'dah stands to garner much esteem from the other city[@1F]states. We would be fools to allow such a golden opportunity to pass us by.

But here's the rub: only by vanquishing Ifrit can our theory be proved. This, [@IF($E1($E9(54),0),[@IF($E3($E9(54),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(54),14)],)],)], is the task we need you to perform. Should you be successful, the sultanate will consolidate its status as Eorzea's foremost city[@1F]state, in scholarly and martial fields both. A single stone to drop two birds, and the honor of casting it will be yours.

Now, you'll be heartened to know that we've obtained intelligence that should facilitate your mission. Our agents have learned that Gridania was recently visited by a most distinguished personage, an elderly Elezen man hailing from Sharlayan.

This fellow─Louisoix is his name─claims to hold the secret to defeating primals. Moreover, he means to strike at Ifrit, and is seeking capable and willing adventurers to assist him. In short, the circumstances could not be more favorable to our cause.
You are to make contact with Louisoix and befriend him. As I mentioned earlier, he is currently sojourning in Gridania, and is regularly seen near Apkallus Falls.

Learn all you can of how to defeat Ifrit, and use the knowledge you acquire to see the deed done. If all goes well, Dalamud will then revert to its former state, and our mission will be a glorious success.

Now, 'tis not without good reason that primals are worshipped as gods in some circles. Before facing Ifrit, you will want to assemble a party of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] able comrades─dependable men and women whom you would trust with your life.
Now, if these loyal allies were to hail exclusively from the ranks of the Immortal Flames, I would see to it that you were further rewarded for your services atop the usual purse.
Why the additional condition, you ask? To that question I respond with another: would you have Ul'dah share her glory with rivals? I thought not.

That concludes the briefing. Now, this is purely routine, but regulations require you to indicate that you consent to undertake the mission. Only then can I consider the task officially assigned. So, go on─let me hear the words.

Hmmm... Not quite what I expected.[@CR]'Tis not a mission for the faint of heart, I'll grant you that. Should you later discover you have the stomach for it, return here once more, and better early than late.

Would you do any less for the glory of your nation? I thought not.[@CR]Make ready then, [@IF($E1($E9(54),0),[@IF($E3($E9(54),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(54),14)],)],)], and depart for Gridania as soon as you are able.
The man we seek, Louisoix, is said to frequent Apkallus Falls in Gridania. I'm told the place is situated along the path to the Lily Hills, the forest city's most affluent district.
For your mission, you are to make contact with Louisoix and befriend him. He is currently sojourning in Gridania, and is regularly seen near Apkallus Falls.

Learn all you can of how to defeat Ifrit, and use the knowledge you acquire to see the deed done. If all goes well, Dalamud will then revert to its former state, and our mission will be a glorious success. I have every faith that you will not fail us.

Your task, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)], is to assist Louisoix directly. Our guest is an elderly Elezen gentleman. Meet with him at Apkallus Falls, and attend well his every word, that you might arm yourself with the knowledge to overcome Ifrit.

Travel to Gridania and seek out the man they call Louisoix. Upon making contact, ascertain if he is who he claims to be, and whether he possesses credible information on Ifrit. Should all appear to be in order, you are to [@1A(1)]invite[@1A(0)] him to Limsa Lominsa.
[@STRING($EB(1))], I presume. Right glad am I to behold at last the valiant adventurer of whom [@SWITCH($E8(1),Y'shtola,Papalymo,Thancred)] has spoken so oft.
Pray allow me to introduce myself. My name is Louisoix Leveilleur, and it is my honor to preside over the Circle of Knowing.

You are yet unfamiliar with our collective, I think. If it please you, the fellowship was formed in Sharlayan, great seat of learning. Ever since our founding, we have endeavored to archive all extant knowledge, that man might learn of his origin and destiny both.

'Tis our firmly held belief that knowledge is power─specifically, the power to realize a better future. To this end, my fellows and I─your friend [@SWITCH($E8(1),Y'shtola,Papalymo,Thancred)] included─have come to Eorzea that we might enlighten her peoples as to what lies ahead.

Mayhap you have also crossed paths with Urianger, yet another of our circle. In which case, I must crave your pardon if his mannerism strikes you as outlandish. 'Tis not his intent to confound folk with cryptic words. You see, the man has seen much more of tomes than he has of the world. I assure you, though, that his heart is in the right place. Ah, but permit me to return to the subject matter at hand.

Just now I made mention of Eorzea's future. But first I must speak of the past, for that which is to come was ever the product of that which has been.[@CR]Ten years ago, an event took place which shook the very foundation of Eorzea: a tribe of beasts summoned forth a primal. So began the spread of summoning till there was not a tribe in this world to whom the practice remained unknown.

Alas, they paid no heed to the consequences of its use. You see, in order to remain in our plane of existence, a primal must needs devour prodigious amounts of aether─the energy bound in crystals and at large throughout all creation.

Consequently, the land is slowly but surely being drained of its aether, and the day fast approaches when the fount will run dry. Should that happen, what then? Why, all life in Eorzea will end. Even as we speak, the land bleeds, with every passing moment another ilm closer to death. And die it surely will─unless we purge it of its blight. Aye, I speak of the primals.
It is to bring about their downfall that I have journeyed to Eorzea. Ifrit, fell primal of the Amalj'aa, shall be the first. I should welcome your help in this.

Forgive me if I seem brusque or presumptuous, but time is not on our side. I require that you procure an echo crystal for each of the six cardinal elements. These crystals have unique reverberative properties, and are yielded only by creatures possessed of an indomitable spirit in life.

Take from me this receptacle, into which the crystals must be placed. Once all six are present, each will begin to resonate with the others, giving birth at last to a new power whose application I shall explain when the time is right.
Now, I have taken the liberty of identifying your quarries. All are creatures of preternatural ferocity, and none will be bested lightly.
The first you will find northwest of Camp Bloodshore in eastern La Noscea. A roseling known by the name of Barometz, it is aligned with the element of wind.
Third, we have the nest commander, an especially savage antling that prowls the area northwest of Camp Horizon in western Thanalan. Its element is earth.
Fifth, we have Queen Bolete, a monarch among funguars, whose element is ice. She holds court southwest of Camp Tranquil in the Twelveswood.

These are the six creatures you must seek out and put down. It matters not the order in which you hunt them, but I urge you to spare no preparation, lest the hunter become the hunted. To make absolutely certain that naught is left to chance, you might consider forming a party of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])].

The second beast also makes its home near Camp Bloodshore, but to the southeast. The people there call it Slippery Sykes, an endearing name for a voracious man-eating slug, I'm sure you'll agree. Its affinity is with water.
Your next quarry is also seen near Camp Horizon, but to the west. A puk called Pyrausta, it is a creature of lightning.
The last is the jackanapes, a fire-aligned primate who prowls the patch of forest southeast of Camp Tranquil.

I require that you procure an echo crystal for each of the six cardinal elements. They are yielded only by creatures possessed of an indomitable spirit in life. I have taken the liberty of identifying six such beasts.

Two more await in Thanalan─one to the northwest of Camp Horizon, and the other to the west. The former is the nest commander, an antling whose element is earth, while the latter is Pyrausta, a puk aligned with lightning.

The last two beasts inhabit areas of the Twelveswood in the vicinity of Camp Tranquil. The first is Queen Bolete, a creature of ice known to hold court northwest of the camp. The second, named the jackanapes, is a fire-aligned primate often seen prowling the forest to the southeast.

All are creatures of preternatural ferocity, and none will be bested lightly. To make absolutely certain that naught is left to chance, you should consider forming a party of [@VALUE(4)] before attempting the deed. Gods willing, I shall see you here again before long─with a receptacle containing six resonating echo crystals, and nary a scratch besides!

In eastern La Noscea you will find Barometz, a creature of wind that inhabits the area northwest of Camp Bloodshore. Southeast of the selfsame camp is Slippery Sykes, a slug whose elemental alignment is water.
It gladdens me to see you returned, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and bearing the echo crystals, no less. 'Tis plain that their power has opened your eyes to the aetherial gate beside me.
You may labor to believe it, but this aetherial gate has always been present─aye, even when you first paid me visit. It was merely veiled from your sight.
There exist objects in the world, you see, that lie beyond the plane of mortal perception. Only by overleaping the boundaries of our senses can such objects be made manifest.

This metaphysical leap may be made via a variety of means, the echo crystals you hold being central to one of them. Indeed, it is they that are responsible for the apparent “appearance” of this particular aetherial gate.
As you are able to see it, so too are you able to traverse it. Ah, but we're not quite ready to step through just yet.[@CR]Would be so kind as to lend me your six echo crystals?

You must needs first summon forth Ifrit, an act which requires [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000419,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000419,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. It serves to kindle a magical flame, you see, which acts as a beacon toward which the Lord of the Inferno may bend his course.

The Amalj'aa Voidtongue Ahzabb Chah is famed as the first of his tribe to summon Ifrit. Greetings, adventurer. You have the look of a seasoned slayer of knaves and ne'er-do-wells. Might you be seeking an opportunity to apply your skills in slaughtery to a cause most noble? Of course you might!

Permit me to explain. A few moons back, our field assessors began to discern a trend in the attacks upon trade ships moored here in Galadion Bay. Now, as you know, random acts of brigandry are hardly uncommon in the city[@1F]state, but this was different─it was...[@1A(1)]predictable[@1A(0)]. Sthalite is a dense, crystalline substance used in goldsmithing and armory, but because it is not readily obtainable on Vylbrand, firms like Naldiq & Vymelli's must import it from Aldenard. The ore is plain in appearance and extremely difficult to refine, making it virtually worthless to all but those with knowledge of metallurgy.

It is well documented that the kobold tribes of Vylbrand are highly skilled in metalworking, with most of their raw materials coming from the countless tunnels carved through the heart of O'Ghomoro. Rarely do they wander far from their caves, shunning contact with Lominsans unless they feel cornered.

The fact that the promise of sthalite drew them out of their holes and into our very midst has prompted us to wonder if the substance might have uses beyond armory and bauble-making...and if those uses might pose a threat to the thalassocracy.

We have taken our concerns to the Maelstrom, and one Chief Storm Sergeant Nolan assured us that an investigation would be conducted shortly. Gridanians have come together as one under the Order of the Twin Adder's banner. Our devotion to the Twelveswood has moved the elementals, and in turn they have bestowed upon us a bounty of gifts.

Speaking of that day, you've probably deduced that I was waiting for Urianger when we chanced to meet. He's a fellow student of the prophesies, you know.
We meet regularly, to keep abreast of each other's findings. Best to do so in a place like this, away from prying eyes.
The Empire has turned its attention to the prophesies, as well. To what end I couldn't say, but it can't be a good one.

Urianger went to great lengths to feed them misinformation. And all the while, my companions and I traveled to the city[@1F]states to meet with their leaders and start the reformation of the Grand Companies.

As far as we can tell, there is not much time left before the onset of the Seventh Umbral Era─and there is so much still to do! I fear we will have need of you again, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and soon.
You should speak to Urianger as well. Well, be spoken to [@1A(1)]by[@1A(0)] Urianger would be more appropriate, I suppose. He's a long-winded old bastard, I grant you, but full of useful tidbits.
Ah, the gods have seen fit to bring thee thus far. Thy reward shall be the sixth verse of the Divine Chronicles.
[@1A(1)]Ne'er till astral hopes dim can umbral dreads fear,[@CR]Waters spout silver swords, skies rain blue spears.[@1A(0)]
[@1A(1)]By ancient truths shall Archons carve men of stone,[@CR]Foe blades chip and shatter, great victories be known.[@1A(0)]

Full many moons have we pored o'er this verse─Papalymo, my own self, and more─yet only now have we discerned its subject. Or think to have. Lest thou wonder in vain, I shall tell thee─it speaketh of the Sixth Umbral Era.
'Twas the sighting of a clay golem, thitherto unseen in Eorzea, that pricked our sleeping senses. What better beasts to play the foretold men of stone?
Yet when the darkness of the Sixth Umbral Era descended, came these automata forth as friend or foe? No man can say. We may yet hazard a guess at one thing, however...

That if their coming signifieth the onset of an Umbral Era, mayhap their disappearance doth the like for its close. For during the darkness between, mayhap life cannot be breathed into mud and rock. But I will not tire thee with further speculation. Let us return to fact.

All now know that the Empire moveth in full force, all semblance of secrecy forgone. Garlemald, in its hubris, would call down the gods themselves that they might defy them. And it is into this faithless morass that these golems of clay now rise.

The Seventh Umbral Era draweth nigh. Even now, its long shadow obscureth the face of this Eorzea. No more is it a distant threat, a riddle within a prophecy of a legend─a thing scarce known and less believed.

So fast upon us is the darkness that mine own master hath pledged to join us here anon, that we may weigh the choices and determine the path to be trod. Long hath he devoted himself wholly to the scriptures, gleaning all therein that might serve us in our hour of need.

He sendeth word that hope remaineth yet. A beacon of radiant light hath he espied, visible on the far horizon, e'en through the blackness of the storm. Should fates permit, I would have thee speak with him. He would be right glad of the chance to meet thee.

Why, askst thou? For thou art the key to our deliverance. The key that openeth the gate unto the world beyond this chaos and ruin. It falleth now to thee to discover that gate, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]─to find thy calling.
The time for thy journey is nigh. Go forth and visit the other great nations, Ul'dah and Limsa Lominsa both. Discover the gate that awaiteth thee, and the path that leadeth from it.
Hearken thou to the words of the Flame General of Ul'dah and the Chief Admiral of Limsa Lominsa both. Discern to what ends their Grand Companies strive. Only then canst thou truly decide.

Perceive not with thine eyes and ears alone, but with thy heart as well. Some truths there are which it alone might descry. Truths most secret, aye, and truths most simple both. Such truths, mark thee, as may yet prove thy salvation.
Tell me, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], hast thou ventured forth unto the great nations? Hast thou found the path thou must walk?
Hearken thou to the words of the Flame General of Ul'dah and the Chief Admiral of Limsa Lominsa both. Discern to what ends their Grand Companies strive. Only then canst thou truly decide.
Now receive of me this gift. May it prove a boon to thee in the war to come.
Ah, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], it is you. I trust you were able to attend the address of Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna? Her words and those of the great ones have touched the hearts of all Gridanians.
Word has reached us of the leaders of the Grand Companies of Ul'dah and Limsa Lominsa giving like speeches.
I pray they, too, will serve to unify the people of their nations, that we might fight together against the Garleans.

Our nations must strive to understand one another. To comprehend not only those things we share, but all things, with sympathy and compassion. That is the key to Eorzea's future. Forgive me. We Gridanians are prone to speak so─flowery and full of hope.

[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I urge you to travel to the other nations, and hear what the leaders of the Maelstrom and the Immortal Flames have to say. Let your understanding begin there, and then let that guide the decisions you must make.

Ah, I've been awaiting your return, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. We received word that the speeches of General Raubahn Aldynn and Chief Admiral Merlwyb Bloefhiswyn were given. Were you present? Come, tell me all there is to know.
I thank you for all you have done, both in Gridania and elsewhere. I trust, though, that your time in the other nations has not...lured you from the path of the Twin Adder.

And yet...I mark in my fellow Gridanians' eyes the same fear that would take the heart of me. These times see great changes in the Twelveswood, and the red of Dalamud grows deeper with each day's passing.

None can say with certainty what is taking place. We know only that it was when Dalamud's visage first took on its bloody hue that the foulness in the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak stirred─a sign most ill.
Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna believes Dalamud to be at the center of all that is happening, and has ordered that thorough studies be made.

The conjurers have taken to the wood, listening for the whispers of the elementals. Men and women of the Wood Wailers, Gods' Quiver, and Garlond Ironworks have begun surveys as well, both within the forest and without.
Ah, but there is more that you must know...yet it is not my place to tell you.
We have dire need of you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]─now more than ever. Please, you must visit Stillglade Fane.
Many of the archers, lancers, and engineers have already assembled there. Seek out Bowlord Lewin. He will explain all.
That is...most unfortunate. Know that our need is real, and pressing. We will welcome you with open arms should you experience a change of heart.
Then go, now. And may the Twelve and the elementals both watch over you.
Recall the words of the great elementals─we must hold to our righteousness and trust to our bravery. So long as we protect our forest, Nophica will never abandon us to the darkness.

I see... That is good. The people of each nation must be brought together before the nations themselves can unite. I only pray that day comes sooner rather than later. In the meantime, you may rely upon me to apprise the Elder Seedseer of that which you have told me.
There is more that you must know...but it is not my place to tell you.
Many of the archers, lancers, and engineers have already assembled at Stillglade Fane. Travel there and seek out Bowlord Lewin. He will explain all.
So you are the adventurer. The one to whom the Twin Adder has seen fit to entrust this task.
So you are the one they call [@STRING($EB(1))]. Well met. I am Lewin, Bowlord of the Gods' Quiver.

You will have seen many of my archers hereabouts, as well as lancers of the Wood Wailers, and engineers of the Garlond Ironworks. All have gathered here at the Elder Seedseer's request, to learn what we might of Dalamud.
We have yet to learn why the lesser moon has taken on its red stain. But we have uncovered one truth that may prove vital.
We were led to it by the whispers of the elementals. They tell us that some moons ago, a great destructive force was sent into the skies.

What is the nature of this terrible power? By what means was it sent? By whom, and to what end? When put these questions, the elementals become terrified, and their whispers turn to silence. And so we have taken another path to seek our answers.
Arthur is one of mine own men─as able as any I have. At my bidding, he has stolen into Ala Mhigo, and placed himself amongst the Garleans.
Why? Because this unknown power, this destructive force, whatever it might be...may very well prove to be the Empire's doing.
We have invited the master of the Ironworks himself, Cid Garlond, to aid us in our investigation. There was some risk in this, but we thought it best he hear the reports of Arthur for himself.
Which brings me to the task we would ask of you.
Meet with Arthur in the clearing to the west of Camp Nine Ivies. Such is as close as we dare draw near the Empire's domain, lest we jeopardize all we have worked for─and Arthur's life besides.
Travel there, and secure the area. There may be beasts, or worse things, but this deed must needs be done.
You've done well, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You needn't worry about Arthur. He has woken, and even spoke with Cid at some length.
It seems Cid now wishes to have words with you. Best not keep him waiting.

We seek a union between Gridania and the Garlond Ironworks. Aye, an unlikely union, I grant you. But it is our very differences that might be made to serve both parties should such an alliance be formed.

Come, you are most welcome, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I have heard all you have done in the service of the Twin Adder. You have proven yourself both capable and loyal, and so it is to you that we have turned this day.

The tragedies to which Arthur bore witness have scarred him. A sad fate, but one shared all too often by those who selflessly serve a greater good. Thanks to his sacrifice, all will now know the atrocities visited upon Ala Mhigo by the Garleans, and that is the most important thing of all.

The Order of the Twin Adder welcomes you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You have been asked to come concerning a task of great secrecy. But few among the Wood Wailers and Gods' Quiver have knowledge of what we aim to do.
The rest has done Arthur well. He is himself again. Still, he will never return to Ala Mhigo. Not after this.
The Order of the Twin Adder has need of every man and woman. Please, find your courage, and serve well.
Things have taken a dreadful turn... Gods, this is all such serious business!
Bowlord Lewin speaks for us all. Mark well his words.
You've seen the deed done, though no celebrations are in order. Still, you should be proud.

Did you hear the address of Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna? Yes? Then I envy you. Mine own duties held me at the airship landing, seeing to repairs. It wouldn't be so bad, but every man, woman and child who [@1A(1)]did[@1A(0)] attend has been singing her praises ever since.
Master Cid visited Arthur after he woke. He returned not long ago, in fact. I...I confess, I found his expression troubling. I can only wonder what Arthur must have told him...

Well met. I am Suzari Sorezari. I have come here in good faith, as an honest man of the Garlond Ironworks, but ever since arriving, I've felt as if I were being watched─[@1A(1)]and not by the people[@1A(0)], if you take my meaning.
Never... Never would I have thought things would come to this.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]? So you are the adventurer sent us by the Order of the Twin Adder.

He painted a godless picture, and I fear the reality of it even worse. A spy must needs smother his own feelings─to deny all that defines him. He had to stand by and watch Ala Mhigans beaten and worked and starved to death. It is enough to drive any man mad...

We are not godless machines, after all. The heart does not always accept what the mind knows. Mayhap it is all the more true for Gridanians. Nowhere have I seen an air of such love and brotherhood amongst a people.
...We must talk of other matters. This fortification of Ala Mhigo, it seems to be the initiative of a legatus newly come to the Eorzean front.

Heavily armored units, new magitek weaponry, extensive drilling of the troops─the Empire is in full motion. Unfortunately, Arthur knew nothing of this destructive force the elementals claim was sent into the skies.
Something big is happening, and not knowing what makes it feel all the more dire.
What is this bloody legatus up to?
I know little and less of this new legatus─this Nael van Darnus...
What the bloody hells is he up to?
I know little and less of this new legatus... Who is this Nael van Darnus? And what of Gaius van Baelsar? What the bloody hells is the Empire playing at?
Those questions will have to wait. For now, I wish to thank you. Arthur would be dead were it not for your efforts.

Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna is appealing to the other two nations to stand together. Even so, many within the Twin Adder are moving to ensure they bring as many capable Serpents to their own banner as possible. I'd wager you'll be offered enlistment sooner than late.

I offer only this by way of advice─think well before swearing yourself to a cause, even one that for all appearances is good. I'll not spout any bloody nonsense about following your heart, but you'll know when it feels right.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], is it not? So you are the adventurer sent us by the Order of the Twin Adder.

Arthur is awake, and suffered me long enough to answer my questions. He is a good man, and a brave soul. He spoke of rapid fortifications being made in Ala Mhigo, and of Ala Mhigans being driven by lash and brand to make them.
I have told those at the Adders' Nest of all you have done.

Why not travel to the other nations and see what it is they have to offer you? I'm sure you'll land on your feet wherever you chance to go. In fact, I'm counting on it. Soon, you adventurers will decide the future of Eorzea, and I, for one, can't wait to see it.
The Adders' Nest welcomes you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
By now you will have seen and heard much in each of the nations of Eorzea. Yet I trust you would agree our Gridania is most virtuous among them.
A [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] of your talent and resolve belongs with the Twin Adder. Come, tarry no longer in the role of recruit. Let us greet you as a true Serpent of the Order.
To pledge yourself to our cause, you must forsake any bonds you have forged with the Maelstrom and the Immortal Flames.
Officially enlisting in the Order of the Twin Adder will delete any recruit status you have with the other Grand Companies.
Duties from the Maelstrom and the Immortal Flames will become unavailable.
You may keep whatever Storm and Flame Seals you have, as they were earned by your own toil. We will not deny you those.
Naught will change with regard to your Serpent Seals, of course. You have my word on that.
There is one more thing...
But believe me when I say that you will have no need of them. The Order of the Twin Adder rewards its leal Serpents, and through service here you will come to know great glories.
Join the Order of the Twin Adder?
You mean to put in with one of the other nations, then? Weaker [@IF($E9(4),women,men)] than you have succumbed to the siren calls of Ul'dah and Limsa. I only pray that you reconsider.
You mean to put in with one of the other nations, then? Weaker [@IF($E9(4),women,men)] than you have succumbed to the siren calls of Ul'dah and Limsa. I only pray that you reconsider.
Then I greet you as a [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)]! The annals of our time shall read that from this day forth, [@STRING($EB(1))] was reborn a Serpent of the Order of the Twin Adder!
The elementals favor you, that much is clear. You will climb our ranks quickly, and your name will one day be spoken throughout the realm. Of that I am sure.

But I speak of things to come. In the here and now, learn what you can from your fellow Serpents. Follow their example, observe and uphold our code, and carry out our tasks to the best of your ability.
The Order of the Twin Adder salute can be performed by selecting Serpent Salute from the emote list, or by inputting the /gcsalute text command.

As you are now one of us, you will find our sutlers have more items to offer you. Your Serpent Seals can now buy you the likes of [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,2001005,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,2001005,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], and more.

With a [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,2001005,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,2001005,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], you will be able to pick a chocobo from the stables. It will serve as your mount, to name as you wish.
We have many and more duties for you to choose from. If you'll allow me, I would be more than happy to detail them.
Ask about which type of duty?

The Order of the Twin Adder is not alone in its use of chocobo caravans. They are essential to the movement of goods across the region. Our birds serve us as well as any man or woman, and so we do not compromise when it comes to their safety. Should you volunteer for caravan security duty, you will be charged with seeing our chocobos safe to their destination, with precious cargo intact.

Surely you now know much and more of the Adventurers' Guild and its guildleves. The Grand Companies have adopted a similar means of delegating tasks, though ours tend more towards direct confrontation with beast and foe.

Provisioning missions involve the procurement and delivery of the raw materials required for the Order's operations. The war effort demands that prodigious amounts of resources be ever ready, of course, but we must needs take care not to tax the forest too heavily.

Supply missions involve the synthesis and delivery of the items required for the Order's operations. We have great need of able crafters. Without the instruments of war, we could wage few battles, and win less.
Very well, then let me speak lastly of our Grand Company currency, the Serpent Seal.

As befits your current rank and station, you are limited to having [@FORMAT([@SHEET(gcRank,11,1)],,)] on your person at any given time. As you perform more duties and distinguish yourself with service, this limit will be raised.
The most rapid way to accomplish this is by ascending the ranks, though bear in mind that a promotion can only be gained after a payment of dues in the form of seals has been made.
The dues vary with rank, of course, but I can say your next promotion will cost you [@FORMAT([@SHEET(gcRank,11,2)],,)] Serpent Seals.
And that, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], is all I have time to tell you. If you would have more, you won't have it from me. I suggest you talk to Lieutenant Sondraix over there.
So go forth, Private [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You are a Serpent now, and the Order of the Twin Adder expects nothing short of greatness from you.
Yet keeping them will yield little benefit. The sutlers in the Hall of Flames and Maelstrom Command will not honor the seals of a sworn Serpent.
The vows of the Twin Adder are for life. Once made, the bond cannot be unmade, nor will you be able to join the Grand Companies of the other nations.
But first, there is something you must know.
Now, I shall teach you the salute of our Order. Come, do as I do.

I have news, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. As you know, Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna has returned to us from the forest. She conducts her divinations tirelessly, granting us new wisdom each and every day.
By her word, it has been decided that a larger force of soldiers, this time from the Wood Wailers and Gods' Quiver both, shall brave the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak in the South Shroud.
The Maws were closed off long ago, but recent reports suggest that someone─or something─had broken the seals and entered the accursed place. And so we sent a unit of Wood Wailers to investigate.

I am sorry to say that most never returned. From what we have since been able to gather, a legion of fiends was waiting for them in the depths─some scouters say their number was over nine thousand, but others say there is no way that could be right.

Ordinarily, I wouldn't give credence to such implausible claims, but Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna sensed the echoes of an impure voice resonating through those foul halls, calling out to beasts across the land and driving them into a blood frenzy...

Many lancers of the first expedition party were tainted with woodsin simply by virtue of being in that damned dungeon, and have since taken ill. The Thousand Maws are cursed indeed. Still, our task must be seen through to the end. Reinforcements must be sent!

Yet stretched though our resources are, I cannot in good conscience send you alone. It would be suicide. For your own safety, assemble a party of [@IF($E5(2,0),[@IF($E2(2,10),[@SWITCH(2,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(2)])],[@VALUE(2)])] to [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] members before heading to the Maws in the South Shroud. The dangers lurking within will permit no less. Will you do this?
Far be it from me to question your decision. But know that this matter is of the utmost importance to the Order of the Twin Adder.
Good. Gather what companions you will, and prepare yourselves for battle. Then travel to the Thousand Maws, north of Camp Tranquil in the South Shroud.
You will find a group of guards stationed near the dungeon's entrance. They will brief you on the situation. Go now, and may the gods go with you.

Foul beasts have infested the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak, and the Wood Wailers alone are not capable of putting them down, such are their numbers. Assemble a party of [@IF($E5(2,0),[@IF($E2(2,10),[@SWITCH(2,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(2)])],[@VALUE(2)])] to [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] members, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Travel north of Camp Tranquil in the South Shroud and aid in their effort.
You will find a group of guards stationed near the dungeon's entrance. They will brief you on the situation. Go now, and may the gods go with you.

Only parties consisting of between [@IF($E5(2,0),[@IF($E2(2,10),[@SWITCH(2,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(2)])],[@VALUE(2)])] and [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE($E8(4))] or above will be granted entry to the dungeon.
Ah, you must be [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. We've been expecting you. Aye, the Nest sent word you'd be coming to help.

But that was not all. We also received urgent orders to locate and extract a Padjal apparently at large in the Maws. To that end, an additional force of Wood Wailers has already entered, accompanied by archers of the Quiver and conjurers of the Fane.

The first Wailer expedition into the Maws was a disaster. We can't say exactly what went on down there, but the party ended up being scattered. It's a miracle any survived. Yet some did, and among them many claimed to have been saved by a Padjal who brought them water and tended their wounds.

Of course, the guards swore that no such soul had entered the dungeon, and assumed the tale to be the delirious rambling of wounded men. But the sheer number of these reports is too great to ignore. If this Padjal [@1A(1)]is[@1A(0)] real, we must do all in our power to see him safely out of the Maws.

You must also keep the following in mind─once you set foot in the Maws, I cannot permit you to re-enter until your body has had time to rid itself of the noxious residues of woodsin and aether which permeate the place.

After completing an expedition in the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak, you will not be allowed to return immediately to the dungeon. To confirm how long you must wait before re-entering, view the Timers tab located under Attributes in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)].

As another measure to prevent the untimely loss of life to the beasts lurking below, I shall be performing a special incantation prepared by the Conjurers' Guild to draw you and your party out of the dungeon after a set amount of time has passed.
You can remain in the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak for a maximum of [@VALUE($E8(2))] minutes (Earth time) per visit.
In addition to my spell, you may leave at any time by returning to the entrance on foot.

There are also rumors of an imperial magitek device located in the farthest reaches of the dungeon. It is said the infernal machine can instantly return a man to this spot, but I am not sure I would trust anything constructed by the Empire. Who knows what sort of havoc the contraption might play on one's humours.

Finally, if you find yourself knocked unconscious by one of the creatures, our scouts have confirmed that using a Return spell will transport you back to the dungeon's entrance, so you may continue your mission, if you so wish.
Until now, our best efforts to investigate the Maws have yielded little and less. Your help is sorely needed. I only hope this mysterious Padjal is found before it is too late.
Go now, and make what preparations you must. When you are ready, come and speak to me again.

Aid the others within, I beseech you. But do not forget the words of the Elder Seedseer. There is a vile voice sounding in those depths, driving those beasts into a murderous rage. You must remain ever vigilant.
Enter the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak?
I understand, and you need not be ashamed of your decision. One must first conquer one's own fears before one can conquer those which trouble others.
It seems you are as ready as you will ever be. Very well. Enter now, and may the Twelve watch over you.
Why, hello there, friend. Are you injured? Lost?
No? What brings you here, then? You're looking for someone? For me?
How did I get in? Why, through the entrance, of course. But please, don't tell anyone. It would only injure the guards' pride─and my sister would be furious besides.
I sensed the moogles were in great danger, you see, and hurried here to save them. It was rash of me, I know, but there was no time to call a council, nor to appeal to the Order of the Twin Adder.
The voices of the crystals are strong here. And of late, I have heard them screaming out in terror from deep below the earth.

All living things are imbued with the power of crystals, and so their screams echo within us all. That is why so many lesser creatures are now crazed and restless. The screams have them in untold agony, driving them to madness.
The moogles are fine, incidentally.
I will leave this place together with them. But for now, I must rest. I am so...weary. I will send word to the Adders' Nest when I can. It was never my intention to trouble them.

Oh, and here─you can have this. The moogles removed it from that magitek device there. I'd take it back with me, but it...it is so...[@1A(1)]heavy[@1A(0)]. I feel it weighs me down...somehow. Take it, please. I cannot carry it a moment more.

This is a strange thing indeed. The elementals tell me that it is attempting to measure the flow of aether through the Maws─though I cannot fathom why a magitek user should deem the stuff sufficiently interesting to warrant such an invention...
You would do well to speak to the moogles, should you know their words. Mayhap there is something to be learned from all of this─some knowledge that may serve my sisters.
I'll rest here just a little longer, but I promise to return with the moogles, and to make all known to the Adders' Nest. It was never my intention to trouble them so.
<yawn> So tiiired...
Kupo!
Goodness gracious me, how embarrassing! To be seen in a place such as this! Wait... You look almost exactly like an adventurer I once met, adventurer.
That's wonderful, kupo! Then I can tell you what happened! A[@1F]Ruhn saved us. I don't know what happened, but one moment we were dancing in our flower fields, and the next we were here.
I think it must have been this strange device. It's too large to move, but I levered off what parts I could. Kupooo...the mere sight of it sends shivers down my spine.
Y-you can understand me!? Are you hearing more than just incomprehensible kupo noises right now?
That's wonderful, kupo! Then I can tell you what happened! A[@1F]Ruhn saved us. I don't know what happened, but one moment we were dancing in our flower fields, and the next we were here.
I think it must have been this strange device. It's too large to move, but I levered off what parts I could. Kupooo...the mere sight of it sends shivers down my spine.
Shudder to think what might have happened if A[@1F]Ruhn hadn't come along! I may have uttered my last kupo!
A[@1F]Ruhn saved us, kupo!
If he hadn't come, we'd be in bloody little chunks for sure, kupo!

This [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000260,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000260,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] is from the device!? Yet another job well done, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].

No doubt you realize by now, but the Padjal you found was none other than Seedseer A[@1F]Ruhn[@1F]Senna, youngest of the three siblings, and brother to Kan[@1F]E and Raya[@1F]O. Gridania is the better for having him back. It was a great thing you did, braving the Maws and convincing him to return.
Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna herself has been informed of your exploits. I can also report that we have made progress in our investigation of the woodsin permeating the Thousand Maws.

The device installed there is of Garlean making. And so the question that concerns us most now is this─how did imperials manage to infiltrate the Twelveswood [@1A(1)]and[@1A(0)] the Maws with such an unwieldy contraption? And all while the elementals looked on! A troubling thought indeed...

Our uncertainty only grew when we were informed of the conjurers' findings. By attuning to the forces within the Maws, they discerned that the device's purpose was to measure the flow of aether in the area. But why should the Empire, with all their infernal technologies, take an interest in that?
If only we could take it─or just a piece of it─to the Garlond Ironworks. Surely the engineers there would be able to glean something useful from it.

From the hands of a moogle to Seedseer A[@1F]Ruhn[@1F]Senna, thence to you, from you to the Order of the Twin Adder, and from us to the Garlond Ironworks! Well, this is no mere coincidence. I do believe our fortunes in this war are changing!

The trees of the Twelveswood are restless, and so too the hearts of men. An ill wind blows across Eorzea, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], unsettling all it touches. Surely you feel it as well.

The Garleans grow bolder by the day. Their soldiers are turning up in nearly every corner of the realm, and ever more frequently. Even more distressing, we've recently learned that control of Dzemael Darkhold in Ishgard has fallen into imperial hands.

Perhaps now you realize the urgency of our situation. Gridania's northern border is at our enemy's mercy. Something must be done. Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna has ordered that able men and women be sent to aid Ishgard on behalf of the Order of the Twin Adder.
Yet there is one remaining matter that worries us...

The Darkhold is a military fortress, and lies not far from the walls of Ishgard itself. Its construction was left incomplete, yes, but even so, the knights of the north would have given their lives to defend it. The Garleans could not have gained entry easily.

Yet gain entry they did, and the knights were slow to counter. Now the imperials are entrenched, and the resources of Ishgard are stretched thin in the effort to oust them from the Darkhold. There must be some sort of explanation for all of this.
It seems Gridania has need of you yet again, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. We must send one of our own to observe the knights closely. Only then may we hope to learn what it is they mean to do.
If you would play your part, make for Owl's Nest in the eastern lowlands of Coerthas. Once there, seek audience with Ser Yuhelmeric, lord commander of knights of House Durendaire.
...I had hoped the obvious urgency of our plight would move you to assist us. Apparently not.
Excellent. But I must warn you─the Darkhold is rife with dangers. Stint not in your preparations.
We are gathering what souls we can to answer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna's call and march north to fight alongside the Ishgardians and retake the Darkhold.

He will grant you entry into the hold─provided you are well accompanied. Head to Owl's Nest in the eastern lowlands of Coerthas. There find a Ser Yuhelmeric, lord of the knights of House Durendaire. He will likely grant you entry to the Darkhold.

Well met, friend. The Order of the Twin Adder sent word that you would be coming.

We were gratified to learn of Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna's promise of reinforcements, but...I must confess, I had not expected them to consist of mercenary adventurers. I take from this that the might of Gridania is dedicated solely to the protection of her own borders.
You have traveled far, and so I shall not do you the disservice of bandying words.

The enemy has not been idle. They command vast legions, and do so masterfully. Reports from the other nations echo our own, with claims of Garlean operatives in nigh on every city, hamlet, and camp in the realm─operatives disguised as adventurers, that their comings and goings might avoid suspicion.

We have seized countless of these brigands attempting to steal their way into the Darkhold ever since the discovery of the crystal veins within. And now here [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] are, the latest fearless adventurer, sent to aid in the heroic reclamation...

You will forgive me, but recent days have bred in me a certain...skepticism. The banner of the Twin Adder lends weight to your claim, but you must still prove yourself both loyal and able. I shall permit you entry into the Darkhold─but require that you slay the Garleans we know to be holding the captain's quarters. Your word is your bond, no doubt, but I shall require [@1A(1)]material[@1A(0)] proof of their demise, nonetheless.
The place you seek will not be reached easily. The foul beasts within will see to that. Yet if you are blessed with ability, and true of purpose, then mayhap the gods will see fit to deliver you.

Also, I will not allow you to attempt this task alone. You may enter as one of a party of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] to [@IF($E5(8,0),[@IF($E2(8,10),[@SWITCH(8,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(8)])],[@VALUE(8)])] members, or not at all. Speak to the guards stationed before the entrance should you wish to know more. I trust you know where the Darkhold... Ahem. I gather from your vacant expression that you did [@1A(1)]not[@1A(0)] know that the Darkhold lies in the central highlands of Coerthas. <sigh> Just go, and gods help us all...

The Black Shroud is ill at ease. You can feel it even from here. I cannot help but wonder if the elementals are hiding something from the forestborn─deceiving them somehow. Of course, such a thought would never cross the mind of a Gridanian.

Business with Ser Yuhelmeric, you say? So the forestborn send a mercenary adventurer to trade words with the lord commander of House Durendaire's knights? <spit> I see those tree-loving arseholes [@1A(1)]still[@1A(0)] haven't learned their bloody courtesies.
The Grand Company of Gridania, risen again. I pray your Order of the Twin Adder proves a powerful ally in the coming struggle.

Count Dzemael himself oversaw the Darkhold's continuing construction. It was to be a great bastion in our war against the dragons. But then the accident happened...and the abominations came. We dare not send men to labor there now, and so it stands incomplete.

I have my doubts as to whether it [@1A(1)]was[@1A(0)] an accident, of course. I make it the work of heretics─sent by the dragons to disrupt the building effort, lest we secure a surer foothold in the highlands.
Take care not to tire within the hold, nor spend all your strength. The ghastly beasts within are large enough as it is. We can ill afford to offer them a free meal! Hahaha!
You represent the Order of the Twin Adder, do you not? I suspected you might. House Durendaire sent word of your coming.
If you truly value your life, then listen carefully to my words.

The depths of the Darkhold are said to contain a rift through which the creatures of the void gain entrance to this realm. And they are not all that passes through. Foul miasmas seep into the caverns, clogging the lungs and poisoning the minds of any who linger too long.

After completing an expedition in the Dzemael Darkhold, you will not be permitted to return to the area immediately. To ensure that the noisome mists are not allowed the opportunity to tighten their grip, I shall be casting a spell upon you that will teleport you back here to my side after the passing of several bells.
