You are free to leave the Darkhold on foot at any time, of course─assuming you remember the way.

Otherwise, it is said there is a magitek device in the farthest reaches of the hold with the power to return a man to this spot in the blink of an eye. I wouldn't go trusting [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] with my worldly being, though.

Oh, and should you come to grief down there, others before you have confirmed that using a Return spell will transport you back to the Darkhold's entrance, so you may continue your mission, if you so wish.
And that is all the information I can give you. If I may offer an opinion, though─this is an evil place, forsaken by the Twelve and embraced by devils. Leave while you still can, and don't look back.
But seeing as you will not, the least I can do is offer you one last opportunity to make your final preparations. Speak to me once more when you are ready.

Enter Dzemael Darkhold?

I had best not discover this was all an elaborate jape at my expense or Twelve help me I will denounce you as a heretic and see you drawn and quartered!
The deed is done? Perhaps I underestimated you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Please, take word of this to Ser Yuhelmeric at Owl's Nest.

It shames me to speak it, but the imperial soldier who carried this may once have been one of our own. Perhaps he turned cloak and fled to the Empire. The lives of such craven traitors are forfeit. All know that the knighthood will hunt them to the ends of the realm, and so, to escape the See's justice, some turn to the Empire, divulging the Darkhold's secrets to curry favor with their new lords.
Come, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I have been awaiting your return. Tell me of your exploits in the north.

Then these so-called isolated incidents in the north are isolated no more. Here, too, we have heard reports of men and women from across the realm defecting to the Empire. But I had imagined them brigands or bandits─not anointed knights entrusted with the secrets of Ishgard!
Ser Yuhelmeric wishes to extend his gratitude once again on behalf of Ishgard. In addition, it seems your distinguished service has earned you the right to enter Dzemael Darkhold as you please.

Ishgard and our own Gridania share a history of animosity. We were once at war, long ago, each nation seeking the annihilation of the other. Yet now we must join forces against a common enemy, lest we share the fate of Ala Mhigo.
But I digress. You have done well to serve in the face of such difficulties, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. The Order of the Twin Adder is truly grateful.
Long now have the wheels of the Garlean war machine been in motion. Yet perhaps those wheels are far grander in scale than any among us had imagined.
Gods, so much armor to make! And [@1A(1)]now[@1A(0)] of all times, when our resources are stretched thinnest...

There was a skirmish between our own forces and those of Garlemald near Fallgourd Lake. Victory was ours, but not without a price.

I speak not of the men we lost. Tragic as it may be, they died in service to the realm, and there is great honor in that. No, I speak of the remnants of the fight left on the field of battle. The leather of all that armor, slashed and pierced and torn...and then carelessly tossed aside.
No battle is without such remains. Experience tells me there are more than a few pieces of armor strewn about up there that could be used for scraps, if not salvaged whole.

It would be remiss of us to abandon that which the forest bestowed. Those leathers are gifts from the animals which gave their lives to make them. We must see that they are treated with the proper respect.

You are of the Twin Adder. Surely you feel the same? Should you happen to find yourself near Fallgourd Lake, do have a look around, would you? If you were able to bring me, say, [@IF($E5(3,0),[@IF($E2(3,10),[@SWITCH(3,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(3)])],[@VALUE(3)])] [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000401,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000401,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], I'd return the kindness.
...Oh. That is a great shame. <sigh> Had the gods granted me a talent for combat, I'd gladly brave the wilds myself. Alas...

Thank you, friend! Just knowing that someone is looking into this will help me to focus on my work here. A word of warning, though─that area is home to dreadwolves, foul beasts with an unslakable thirst for blood.

Yet through all those births and deaths, the essences of things are not changed at all. She said that when we come to know that─[@1A(1)]truly[@1A(0)] know it─then our eyes will be opened.

I was too intent on my duties to even take notice... I saw the cost of everything, yet the value of nothing. Yet now I see that I am here now because of life's march─its cycle. That I am the same as those scraps of leather, part of a far greater whole.

And so I shall take these precious [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000401,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000401,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] you have placed yourself in harm's way to gather, and from them fashion new armor to protect those who fight under our banners! She thought it was wrong of me to ask you to go to such a dangerous place─and so shortly after a confrontation with the Garleans. I count my blessings that you are safe, truly.
Well, if it isn't [@STRING($EB(1))]! I hear you've been made a Serpent of the Twin Adder─though why such a fine force would welcome the likes of you is beyond me. Hah hah!

We Wood Wailers have been called upon to serve as well, as has the Gods' Quiver under Bowlord Lewin. Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna herself has put to us the task of training recruits. Theirs is the only green this wood has no use for.
Most have never wielded a spear nor donned a jerkin. A far cry from you adventurers, but they mean well enough.
Even so, there is one among them, Hilith, who is proving most...troublesome. Her passion for the cause is unquestionable, to be sure. Greater than most, in fact. Yet...
The woman is hopeless with a spear, and makes no effort to improve. She has little love for drilling, and less for rules. Hells, even now she is off to gods know where without my leave.
I've put in for her discharge on more than one occasion, but my commander won't hear of it. He says the fault lies in my leadership.
I mean to make commander myself someday, and I'm not about to let an upstart recruit put an end to my hopes. I must find the [@IF($E9(4),girl,wench)] and make a true Wailer of her!
You have better things to do, is that it? Then bloody be off and about them!

But I can only cover so much ground on my own... Would you help me? If you could search for her near the Rootslake in the South Shroud while I scour Quarrymill Landing, I would consider it a great service.
It's always an honor to meet a Serpent of the Twin Adder. You're in exalted company, there. The Order's home to many of the realm's finest.

How can I train those who would protect the realm, if I cannot even train a green girl? ...Bah! I shall not give in to doubt. Hilith is an unruly mare to be broken and tamed. But first, she must be found.
I will look for her at Quarrymill Landing. Please, search near the Rootslake in the South Shroud. If you find her, put the fear of the gods in her, will you?

Begging your pardon, I know your name but I've yet to give you mine. I am Challinie, conjurer of Stillglade Fane, medium of the Lancers' Guild, and dear friend of Hilith. It was I who put forth her name for recruitment.
And I would again, despite the worst of Dhemdaeg's protests. I've never known a person of greater convictions or dedication.

She often speaks of the gaze he fixes her with. Cold and steely and filled with loathing, as she tells it, and enough to sap the strength from her knees. All because he sees her as naught but an obstacle to his own petty ambitions. Such a shame.

It is true her talents do not lie with the spear. But there is more to service than spears. The girl is charismatic and clever. She warms the spirits of those around her, and has a profound love for both nature and nation.

There is none more fit for service than she. If Dhemdaeg cannot see that, then it is he who is unfit to lead. Who we meet in this life is the work of the gods. But once met, it falls to us to bring out the best in each other.
I think it high time the truth came out. Here, look at this. It is a drawing of me, done by Hilith herself. Rather good, is it not?
Ah, so it is another purpose that has brought you. Dhemdaeg? Searching for one of his recruits, you say? A girl named Hilith?

I am sorry you came all this way, friend, but Hilith has already returned to the Wailing Barracks. She was with me, yes, practicing her spearwork. But I dared not bring her here. She is not quite ready for such a fight.

She often retreats to the wood and takes to drawing after being chided. I want you to show that drawing to Dhemdaeg, and tell him all I have told you. Perhaps it will help the fool realize that some gifts in this world do not lie at the end of a spear haft.

But she also has the pride of youth. She would not let the others see how unwieldy she is with a spear. And yet she has the fears of a recruit, as well, and cannot bring herself to ask Dhemdaeg's leave to train alone.

You, there! You are a Serpent of the Twin Adder, are you not? The wood's whispers told of a foul beast here, and so I came to put it down. But I see you have already done it for me. You have my thanks for that.
I think it high time the truth came out. Here, look at this. It is a drawing of me, done by Hilith herself. Rather good, is it not?

Ah, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], you're back. It seems Hilith returned not long after you and I departed. Somehow that girl manages to waste my time even when she's not present. I was just on my way to have words with her.

The merchant's name is Taylor. He can be found at the docks where the ferries from Limsa Lominsa put in. Persuade him to assist us, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and the Immortal Flames may well greet you as a [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)] when next you come.
He can be found at the docks where the ferries from Limsa Lominsa put in. Win us his trust and allegiance─and most importantly, his gil!
Without men of influence like Taylor, the Immortal Flames' cause is as good as lost. Do whatever it takes to win his support, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].

If what I've heard is true, you're most likely to find Urianger near these very docks. Head just southeast of here and odds are you'll come upon him before long.
If I'm going to turn this hunch into profit, though, I'll first need information! I must know precisely what is transpiring. So go and find this Urianger, and bring him to me─by force, if you must.

Haha, you would do well to learn the value of perspective, my friend. Where others see danger, I see potential! To them, fear, to me, fortune! I smell an opportunity here, but I need to know the details before I can act.
Time is money. Go now, just to the south and east of here. You're like to find this Archon named Urianger at these very docks.
Well, look who it is. I confess I was just asking myself whether you would return. Have you found our good Urianger, then?
Escaped...? Gods, this bastard is more elusive than a greased opo[@1F]opo. I thought an adventurer perhaps capable of the task, but it seems I was wrong.

Bah, there is no use nor gil in lamenting over such failures. You were able to procure some new information, so your efforts were not entirely lost. This Hyur bloke you spoke of seems to know quite a bit about the Umbral Eras.

The question I now find myself asking is whether all of this was mere coincidence. Hmmm...I think perhaps that I should inform my superiors. I am not one to ignore my instincts─it is they that have made me a rich man, after all.

You failed to fulfill the task I set before you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Still, you are not wholly undeserving of some praise for your show of sincerity and diligence. Allow me to give you a second chance.
I am willing to fund the Immortal Flames... But I shall give to them only so much coin as they give power to me. You may tell that barbarian Raubahn those are my terms.

I am willing to fund the Immortal Flames... But I shall give to them only so much coin as they give power to me. Now run along to the headquarters of the Flames, and tell that barbarian Raubahn those are my terms.
Welcome back, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Tell me, how did you fare? You carry a letter from Taylor? Show me...

So, he demands power to command the Flames in exchange for his gil... I suppose we should have expected as much. I will see to it word reaches Flame General Raubahn─both of this and of your loyal service.
As for enlistment in the Immortal Flames, it is I who have been entrusted to make final decisions regarding recruits. Come and speak to me again if you are still interested. That is all.

What preparations there were are now complete, and the Immortal Flames have been rekindled. Even now, we are carrying out operations across the region. I would like to offer you the chance to join the Immortal Flames as a recruit, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].

So which will it be? Will you join us and oppose the Garleans in the name of freedom? Or will you cower as other brave souls step forward to fight this war for you?
Join the Immortal Flames as a provisional recruit?
So be it, but our doors shall remain open. You know where to find us should you [@IF($E9(4),have a change of heart,locate your manhood)].
A wise and noble decision. I have no doubt that you will achieve greatness marching under our banners.
And now, duty requires that I speak to you of our Grand Company seals.

Our stores contain items made by the finest artisans and craftsmen in Ul'dah. But they are available only to those deemed worthy of the Immortal Flames, and only then through the exchange of seals earned through faithful service.
You are no stranger to the ways of this nation. With enough gil, one can buy power, fame, love. Just so with our seals. They can be used to purchase more than mere items.
But know that only our own Flame Seals are accepted here. Those of the Grand Companies of Limsa Lominsa and Gridania will not be honored.
What's that you say? You'd like to get your hands on some of these seals? Hahaha!

Well...I suppose I could stand to part with a few, given your obvious enthusiasm. After all, I'm [@1A(1)]sure[@1A(0)] you will be joining our Immortal Flames at the first opporunity. Isn't that right?
Now, do you see that lovely Miqo'te standing just next to me? That is Flame Sergeant First Class Rahz, and she knows all there is to know of seals. Speak to her if you wish to learn more.

I am Flame Sergeant First Class U'sanzi Rahz. Allow me to congratulate you on your provisional enlistment in the Immortal Flames.
I am responsible for the issue of gear and items, but only to those in possession of Flame Seals─the currency of our company. You are new to us. Tell me, do you require any further explanation?

The Immortal Flames have established this store so that its members might use their Grand Company seals to purchase various gear and items. We have taken special care to amass those articles we feel will be most appreciated by you adventurers. The items available to you as a provisional recruit are limited, however.
When the time comes for you to pledge yourself fully to the Immortal Flames, and win great victories under her banners, you will find ever more impressive gear available to you.
But that is not all. Your Flame Seals can also be used to raise you through the ranks of our organization. There are other privileges beyond this, as well.
But entry into our ranks does not come easily─it must be earned. If you have undertaken any tasks at the behest of First Flame Lieutenant Aubrey, then you know of what I speak.

We wish to bring only the most dedicated and loyal of adventurers into the Immortal Flames. Our Grand Company is a symbol of Eorzean freedom. We put these duties to recruits to weed out the weak and the unworthy.
Only after you succeed in carrying out the tasks put to you, and are deemed worthy of the honor, will you be welcomed as one of our own─as one of the Immortal Flames.

I should also mention that officially enlisting in the Immortal Flames will cost a certain amount of company seals. But worry about crossing that bridge when you come to it. For now, I urge you to exchange what seals you have here for [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3020204,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,3020204,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)].
They will prove most useful while fulfilling the tasks put to you by First Flame Lieutenant Aubrey.
Inquire further?
So new to our ranks and yet already so familiar with our ways? Somehow I doubt it.
You have come to aid the cause? That is good. I have an urgent task for which I require a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] of your proven loyalty.
A unit carrying arms and munitions from near Ala Mhigo has come under attack. It would appear that the Garleans have blockaded the trade route.
That route is Ul'dah's lifeline to the East, and carries the bulk of our trade. If we lose it, it will cost the nation billions, and effectively neuter our military.
Should it come to that, we would lack the strength to withstand a direct attack. We must break the Garlean blockade. We [@1A(1)]must[@1A(0)]!

We have learned what we can of the imperials holding the road. They are known as the Hellhounds. According to our intelligence, they have taken up a position close to the Golden Bazaar. You must depart as soon as you are able.
I...understand. This is not a task to be taken lightly. The Hellhounds are notorious for their savagery. It is said even among the Garleans they are known as the Empire's “mad dogs.”
Then return to us only after you have seen the thing done. The Immortal Flames will not accept failure.
The route blockaded by the Empire's Hellhounds is Ul'dah's lifeline to the East. It was established by Lord Lolorito, and has brought great profit and prosperity to our nation.

Surely you know of Lord Lolorito. No individual is more influential in Ul'dah's trade than he. Not only is he head of the East Aldenard Trading Company, but he holds a seat on the Syndicate as well. He is one of the richest and most powerful men in all the realm.

The clothing and accessories handled by the East Aldenard Trading Company enjoy popularity throughout the realm. Lord Lolorito has invested a great deal in the development of the eastern route, and has a say in all the goods that move along it.
I have received word of your deeds from our scouts in the field. You have done exceptionally well.
The lawless fiends ran rampant under the protection of the imperial banner, pillaging and plundering. It was only when Lord Lolorito bribed the scoundrels that the safety of the road was restored.
Unfortunately, that provided the Empire with an excuse to march on east Thanalan, ostensibly to put down their rogue Hellhounds.

If that happens, we will be forced to rely almost exclusively on sea routes through Limsa Lominsa. Yet the Empire is making its presence felt there as well, and the situation grows more unstable by the day.

It won't be long before the Garleans impose a sea blockade─assuming the threat of war doesn't force the Lominsans to close their ports first. It makes little difference, of course─either one would mean an end to shipping.

There is no more time to explain. Head west to the ferry docks and seek passage to Limsa Lominsa. There you are to secure us a contract with no fewer than [@IF($E5(3,0),[@IF($E2(3,10),[@SWITCH(3,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(3)])],[@VALUE(3)])] famous arms dealers.
These Hellhounds may march under the Empire's banner, but they are in truth no more than honorless sellswords, hired to harry our borders.
Naught but lies and posturing, of course, but we will likely be forced to abandon the route all the same.
Yet ours is a mercantile nation. Without trade, we are nothing. We must reclaim the eastern trade route, before all hope is lost. And to that end, we must equip ourselves.

If worst comes to pass, the Garleans will attempt to blockade trade routes over both land and sea. Needless to say, we cannot allow that to happen─yet we lack the weapons to prevent it. I need you to travel to Limsa Lominsa, and secure for us arms contracts with [@IF($E5(3,0),[@IF($E2(3,10),[@SWITCH(3,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(3)])],[@VALUE(3)])] dealers.
So, come to Woolvale Arms lookin' for a contract, have ye?

Them Garleans've cast their net o'er all Eorzea, and every day sees it drawn tighter about us. Most folk here reckon they mean to raze the whole bloody realm to the ground. Hells, merchants from across the seas have already put an end to their dealin's here.
But there ain't no business like war, and no business partner like Lord Lolorito. If it be arms ye're after, Woolvale'll be happy to oblige ye.
Who ye representin'? The East Aldenard Tradin' Comp'ny? Hah! That Lolorito don't wait around, does he!? S'pose that's to be expected, though, seein' as how he's got more gil than the gods.

Gridania's right on the Empire's doorstep, and Lominsan regulations are too bloody strict by half, so Woolvale's more than pleased to enter into terms with the honest folks o'er at the East Aldenard Tradin' Comp'ny.
The East Aldenard Trading Company seeks to deal in arms with us? Teeheehee!

Still, Lord Lolorito's successes speak for themselves, as does his influence. The man genuinely has a gift for the merchant's trade. Speaking of which, is it [@1A(1)]true[@1A(0)] what the smallfolk say? Does Lord Lolorito [@1A(1)]really[@1A(0)]...

...shit gil? Teeheehee! I jest, of course! Gods, please don't tell him I said that! Of course we will enter into a contract with the good lord! Straight Edge Traders would be [@1A(1)]honored[@1A(0)] to do business with the East Aldenard Trading Company.
But of course it does. Lord Lolorito is the proprietor of the Eshtaime and Sunsilk names, and still others besides. Purveyors of such opulent goods are always first to feel the pinch in times of war.
If it is arms Lord Lolorito seeks, Straight Edge Traders will be happy to deliver. You have our word. Teeheehee!
We are always honored to welcome an emissarrry from the East Aldenard Trading Company. All know that dealings with Lord Lolorito have never yet failed to yield a profit!
He will have the contract he seeks. The Gigas Forge is at your serrrvice.
We have been praying for the day an opportunity such as this would come along. The Gigas Forge is at your serrrvice!
You were able to secure all of the contracts? Well done, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! I see your bravery is matched by your powers of persuasion!
I have some good news, as well. We were able to agree to terms with the Garleans. The trade route to the East has been named a demilitarized zone. Shipping will continue safely, for now.
It should come as no surprise to hear it, but Lord Lolorito was not sitting idly by while the road was being lost. I shudder to think what sums exchanged hands to secure this superficial peace...

But there is no need to worry. Whatever money was lost will soon be made back tenfold. While the other nations have already begun to limit their trade, Ul'dah has seized near complete control of the flow of arms─and this upon the eve of war!
And so you see what it is that makes Ul'dah great─the ability to find fortune in every misfortune.

The Garlond Ironworks is producing the finest weaponry in the realm, and we mean to make them the most sought-after goods on the market! Being a member of the Immortal Flames, these weapons will of course be at your own disposal as well, should you rise high enough in our ranks.
I trust you are finding service to the Immortal Flames rewarding? Yes, we Ul'dahns know the value─and cost─of good [@IF($E9(4),women,men)] such as yourself.

That lot? Don't get me wrong, we are grateful to Ul'dah for their aid, but...

That lot didn't have much of a mind for cooperating. We asked that they wait a spell before heading into the Thousand Maws. One does not simply go storming into a place thought so tainted with evil as to be sealed by the conjurers.
They made themselves scarce after that, and then disappeared altogehter. If I were to venture a guess, I'd say they'd gone off and into the Maws of their own accord, the bloody fools.

The Maws are a labyrinth of twisting tunnels and shafts, and break the surface in more places than one. Our eyes cannot be everywhere at once. It is possible they found another way in. It would not be the first time, nor the last, I venture.
There is even talk of moogles leading folk to secret entrances, though what possesses the furry little bastards is a mystery to me.

Whatever came of the Ul'dahns, I can't bloody well say if they are even in the Maws. You seem confident that they are. It might be you are privy to some knowledge I am not. But I don't much care in any event. You'll have to brave the Maws yourself if you wish to search for them.
The beasts within are in a frenzy the likes of which we've never seen in the Twelveswood. I will not refuse you entry, but I must insist on certain conditions.
Once you set foot in the Maws, I cannot permit you to re-enter until your body has had time to rid itself of the noxious residues of woodsin and aether which permeate the place.

That is all I can tell you for now. The truth is that we, too, are not fully apprised of the situation─including the role of the moogles in all this. We will provide you with what support we can, but you'd be wise not to let your guard down once inside.

It is an admirable thing, wishing to help one's brethren. But if you are unsure of your mettle, perhaps it is best you not enter.
You are an adventurer, yes? I wonder, kupo...can you understand me? Are you hearing more than just incomprehensible kupo noises right now?
You are looking for your friends? How touching! You adventurers are all best friends forever, kupo!
Oooh, maybe this belongs to one of your friends, kupo? I found it deep, deep in the dungeon. But you mustn't go there! I saw Garleans! Garleans and more Garleans!
Your friends... I think perhaps they are... Well, they're dead, kupo.

I don't know what happened. One moment we were dancing in our flower fields, and the next we were here. That's when I noticed your friends, kupo. They must have seen the hidden entrance we used in the forest and followed us!

Anyway, it was then that I heard a strange voice, kupo. It sent a shiver right down my spine. Not long after that, we found this contraption here. Your friends started poking and picking at it, kupo. Maybe it was this strange device that brought us here... That called to us...
I pulled this bit off it, but now I've got a very, very bad feeling, kupo. Here, please take it far away from here. Far, far away!
Now, I'll just have a little nap and then be on my way. No need to worry about me, kupo.
Goodness gracious me! You look almost exactly like an adventurer I once met, adventurer. I wonder, kupo...can you understand me? Are you hearing more than just incomprehensible kupo noises right now?
I'll just have a little nap and be on my way. No need to worry about me, kupo. I'm feeling a bit better now, thanks to A[@1F]Ruhn.
He saved us! A[@1F]Ruhn saved us!
It was the voice. We couldn't resist it, kupo! A[@1F]Ruhn told us it was the crystals crying out.
Just what is this horrible contraption doing to the crystals?
So you have escaped the Maws with your life─no small feat, that. Tell me, what did you discover within?
Garleans... I see. And your missing friends? Ah. It is as I feared. I am sorry for Ul'dah's loss.

There is much to consider. The power of this mysterious voice, for example. For it to summon beasts is one thing─but moogles? And this magitek device...if it is indeed of Garlean making... What does it all mean? We must investigate further.

I will see that Nuala is informed of everything. I ask that you refrain from speaking of this to any of my countrymen. We must not let unconfirmed information disseminate amongst the people. That will only lead to panic.
On behalf of Gridania, I thank you. The information you have provided may prove crucial to understanding the Empire's plans for my nation, and Ul'dah as well.
I see... At the hands of imperials, you say? I am sorry. That is...most tragic.

But their death was not in vain. Both they and you have learned much of great value. This magitek device that appears to be of Garlean making, and its influence over the moogles... But what is the connection?

We must carry out further investigations if we are to understand all of this. Until we do, I must ask that you not let word of this spread to the masses. We cannot afford the panic. I will send word to Nuala myself.

I will see that Nuala is informed of everything that has happened. I ask that you refrain from speaking of this to any of my countrymen. We must not let unconfirmed information disseminate amongst the people. That will only lead to panic.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! It is good to see you in the Hall of Flames once more. Tell me, were you able to find our soldiers?
This bracer belongs to... No. Dead? All of them? But they were some of our most battle-hardened warriors! What evil could have done such a thing?
Garleans!?

I would not have thought the Gridanians capable of concealing information of such import. And now it has cost us the lives of many good men. Had we known, we may have pursued another course of action.
We will keep this bracer, in memory of our fallen. At least you have returned to us with your life. Thank the gods for that.

As for this [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000262,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000262,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], you claim it to be part of a magitek device placed within the Maws by the Garleans? This bodes ill...all of it. Hordes of feral beasts, Garlean soldiers, a strange voice that unmans even moogles... Just what in the bloody hells is going on in that damnable dungeon!?

The Immortal Flames will not stand idly by. This is a time for action. And to act we must have information─such as the kind you have brought us this day. You have done well, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and shall be rewarded.
Limsa Lominsa, too, must be informed of this. The three nations must devise a strategy together.

[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], again you honor us with your visit. And again I have a task for you.

Many years ago, the Ishgardians undertook to build a mountain fortress in the central highlands of Coerthas. They called it the Dzemael Darkhold. Regretfully, we have learned that it has fallen under Garlean control.
As if that were not troubling enough, our scouts report seeing a high-ranking officer amongst the imperial forces stationed there─a man we believe to be the Legatus of the VIIth Legion.
In case you are unaware, the hold takes its name from House Dzemael, one of the four high houses of Ishgard. It was they who were responsible for its construction and subsequent defense...

Clearly, they were no match for the might of the Empire. But then who alone could claim to be? Perhaps it was this realization that drove them to put away their pride and take up arms with the other high houses. Together, they were able to retake the Darkhold's main gate.
Those come from the city are at Owl's Nest in the eastern lowlands of Coerthas. From there, they have sent messengers into the high mountains to deliver the call to arms.

When the call is answered, the army of House Fortemps will be flooded with unknown faces. Think of it─none will contest the presence of complete strangers. If ever there were a time to plant a spy to the north, that time is [@1A(1)]now[@1A(0)]! We must learn what we can of the Darkhold, and of Garlean operations in the area.

The Flames would send you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Travel to Ishgard and take part in the attempt to reclaim Dzemael Darkhold. The commanding officer of House Fortemps's army is Ser Artoirel. You will first need to present yourself to him for duty.

For years now, Ishgard's gates have been closed to outsiders. Never have we seen such an opportunity to place one of our own in their midst, and we do not intend to let it pass by. If you will not serve us, we will find another who will.

Excellent. Then head north until you are among the knights, and look for the unicorn─the sigil of House Fortemps. Seek out this Ser Artoirel, and present him with this [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000265,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000265,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)].

But the structure is vast, and built around naturally occurring caves and tunnels. There are not men enough to secure all points of entry. And so another of the high houses, House Fortemps, has appealed to the knights of Ishgard's outer regions to join the fight.
Travel to Ishgard and take part in the attempt to reclaim Dzemael Darkhold. Learn whatever you can of what lies within, and of the Garleans who have seized control.

Knights of House Fortemps have been dispatched to Owl's Nest. You seek Ser Artoirel? On what business?

So you bear a [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000265,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000265,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. Are you the [@IF($E9(4),daughter,son)] of a swineherd, then? <sigh> It would seem our desperation knows no bounds. Well met, country bumpkin. You have the honor of speaking to Ser Vairemont of House Fortemps.
I cannot present you to Ser Artoirel because he is not here. He has ridden for the front with the main body of our force.

If you wish to distinguish yourself with service, hurry to the Darkhold in the central highlands. Show that [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000265,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000265,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] of yours to the knights at the main gate. They will grant you entry.

But know this─the latest reports show that it is not only Garleans infesting the Darkhold. There are all manner of beasts and monsters roaming those halls, as well. The kind that take bumpkin sers for tasty morsels, hahaha!

Ahem. Storm the Darkhold with your brethren, and put down whatever imperials you encounter within. Return with proof of their demise, and you shall be generously rewarded─with more than you're like to see in a lifetime in Norwick, I should imagine.

He departed the instant we received word that Nael van Darnus, Legatus of the VIIth Legion, had been sighted amongst the Garleans' ranks.

An enemy pincer action had seen our men surrounded, and they were able neither to press forward nor retreat.

We had heard that Nael van Darnus was a cunning leader in battle, and a gifted tactician. Should you find him, I warn you not to confront him directly. Such recklessness will only serve to make the Darkhold your tomb.

If you truly value your life, then listen carefully to my words. The depths of the Darkhold are said to contain a rift through which the creatures of the void gain entrance to this realm. And they are not all that passes through.

Foul miasmas seep into the caverns, clogging the lungs and poisoning the minds of any who linger too long. Those who have entered the hold are therefore advised to wait for a period of several suns to allow the taint to quit the body before attempting another foray.

Oh, and should you come to grief down there, former visitors have confirmed that using a Return spell will transport you back to the Darkhold's entrance, so you may continue your mission, if you so wish.
And that is all the information I can give you. If I may offer an opinion, though─this is an evil place, forsaken by the Twelve and embraced by devils. Leave while you still can, and don't look back.

Your deeds have brought great honor to House Fortemps. Go now, Vairemont awaits your report at Owl's Nest.
It seems I underestimated you. Your bravery in the Darkhold brought many of our men back alive. Ser Artoirel himself saw fit to praise your deeds.

This is [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000266,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000266,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]! The helm of a legatus! Its design is unmistakable. But that would mean...
Y-You... Twelve be good, could it be? You've slayed Nael van Darnus!

...Is no doubt what you wanted to hear. Am I not right, Ser Bumpkin? The truth of it is that scores of men have brought me countless of these false helms upon their return from the Darkhold. So many, in fact, that I am heartily sick of seeing them!

You fools from the country have much to learn. The Garleans often employ this tactic. The corpse you prized this helm from was but one of many decoys─men clad to resemble the Legatus in order to protect him. A crowd for that craven to cower behind.

Ser Artoirel, too, was vexed by this. He pursued van Darnus and his men into the Darkhold, only to be flanked by another force led by another van Darnus! Gods know how many doppelgangers the bastard has!

We have spies who have infiltrated the Empire. From their reports, we know that the Legatus is a man of great intellect, but also great cruelty and savagery. We know that he is feared among the Garleans. And yet we do not even know if he was among those we pursued into the Darkhold.

It may well be that van Darnus was simply toying with us, laughing all the while from behind the safety of Garlean lines. Yet the knights of Ishgard do not make excuses. We were bested this time around.

But we will not let ourselves be fooled again. Not by the likes of van Darnus, nor by the likes of you. Aye, Ser Bumpkin, your lies have been exposed. Another among our ranks hails from Norwick. After hearing you in passing, he claims you do not speak the region's dialect.

If it were left to me, I'd have you chained to a stone in the mountains as dragon bait. But none can deny the merit of your deeds in the Darkhold. Whatever lies you've told, you saved the lives of many of our men. It is for Ser Artoirel to decide your fate, anyway, and he has ordered you be set free. Now be gone from my sight, false knight.
Still, Nael van Darnus escaped us. It seems the Legatus is as crafty when retreating as he is when attacking.
Decoys, the whole bloody lot! And we ran headlong into their trap, as the fox after the hen! Van Darnus has made fools of us all!

I take it the deed is done? You see, we received a parcel not long ago, addressed to you care of the Flames. It contained a gold nugget and a note complimenting your incomparable valor and distinguished service...marked with no less than the seal of House Fortemps.

And lucky for us, as well. This could easily have ignited tensions between our nations. A narrow escape, indeed. Oh, I should probably mention that we've taken the liberty of exchanging your nugget for Flame Seals. Now, tell me all that you have learned.

Then it is just as we thought. The Garleans have deployed a magitek device within the Darkhold, yes, but what we must ask is why [@1A(1)]there[@1A(0)]? Of all the places in all the realm, why did they choose [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] precise location?

It seems to me now that the answer lies with the crystals. Dzemael Darkhold lies atop lands once prized by all the nations for their high crystal content and mining potential. The Empire must covet them for the same reasons.
Yet I cannot fathom why they should... Ceruleum is the fuel needed to drive their magitek. To what end would they crave crystals?
And if our reports are to be believed, the Legatus of the XIVth Legion has now been seen at the Darkhold as well. It appears the Empire has no intentions of losing control of it.

We will have to continue our investigations at the Darkhold to determine precisely what it is the Garleans are after. No doubt we will call on you again, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. For now, though, your duty is fulfilled. Well done.

Traveling from one end of Eorzea to the other and speaking with the same accent... You must have taken leave of your bloody senses! Did you honestly think you wouldn't be discovered!? Lucky for you, your deeds spoke louder than your distinctly unconvincing words. Ser Artoirel has ordered that your crime of impersonating a knight of Ishgard be pardoned.
